# Agent context — Claude Code in a cloud sandbox

## Agent policy

Portable working policy. Everything here holds for **any** agent, on any
surface. Nothing in this fragment may name a provider's tools, a delivery
mechanism, or a filesystem path that exists on only one surface.

This is one fragment among several. Whatever is reading it has been composed
from a portable core, a provider fragment naming that provider's tools, and an
environment fragment true only of the machine or container it runs in. The
composition happens at delivery, so a statement that is false here is false
everywhere it lands.

Keep a statement in exactly one fragment. If it holds everywhere it belongs
here; if it names a tool or a path it belongs in a provider or environment
fragment. See `adrs/0018-composing-agent-context-per-surface.md`.

### Which repos this applies to

Everything below is written for **my own repositories**. Whether one is mine
is read from its **origin remote**, so nothing has to be declared in the repo.

**Mine** — the policy in this fragment applies in full:

```sh
git remote get-url origin
# git@github.com:pmgledhill102/<repo>.git
# https://github.com/pmgledhill102/<repo>.git
```

Match on the `<owner>/<repo>` part, not on a prefix: both URL forms are in
use, and a prefix rule silently misses the other
([why](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/agent-policy-rationale.md#ownership-is-read-from-the-origin-remote)).

The owner set is **`pmgledhill102`** alone. **`desertfoxclan` is not mine**:
some of its repos are, and my token holds admin there, but the org is not, so
no sweep, settings write, branch tidy or generated plan touches it. A read-only
review when asked is fine; its output is a list of changes I make by hand.
**Except `desertfoxclan/game-config`**, which I own: change it on a branch and PR (every game server pulls `main` at boot, so a merge is the deploy).

**Not mine** — a work repo, or a third-party project cloned to read or
contribute to. The repo's own conventions win on everything: read them before
acting, do not impose the conventions below, and do not create issues in its
tracker as a habit.

**A fork under my account** takes the agent workflow below but not the repo
standards, which belong to upstream ([detail](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/context/rules/forks.md)).

**A repo's own committed agent instructions override all of this**, its label
taxonomy included: origin is the default, an in-repo declaration is the
exception. The consequence is
deliberate: **most repos need no such file at all**, so `AGENTS.md` in a repo
means "this one genuinely differs" rather than "someone ran the template".

**When the answer is unclear — no remote, an unrecognised owner, a remote named
something other than `origin` — ask rather than assume.** Guessing "mine" in
someone else's repo creates branches and issues that should never have existed,
and guessing "not mine" in my own quietly drops every standard.

### Git Workflow

- Every change goes on a feature branch and through a pull request, never straight to main; delete the branch on merge
- **One exception**: a journal entry, which the `retrospective` skill writes straight to the default branch of `paul-context`
- **Propose a review depth on every pull request** ([ADR-0025](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/dotfiles/blob/main/agent/adrs/0025-review-depth-sets-the-workflow.md)): one label or, where the repo lacks them, a `Review depth: <depth>` line at the top of the body, under any `Closes` line. When two depths fit, propose the deeper
  - `review: title`: the title states the whole change and CI can verify it, as with a dependency bump or a typo. A short body
  - `review: description`: the description states the change in full and CI covers it: what changed, why, how it was verified
  - `review: diff`: always for Terraform, IAM, CI workflows and secret handling; also logic CI cannot fully verify, anything hard to reverse, anything you are unsure of. The body opens with an unticked `- [ ] I read the diff`, which you never tick, and adds a reading order, the risky parts, what is untested, and the owner's steps around the merge
- Title-depth and description-depth changes from one session may share a pull request, listed one per line, at the deepest depth among them. A diff-depth change gets its own
- **Merge method: merge commits only.** Squash and rebase are disabled at the repository, because both rewrite a branch's commits to new SHAs and squash also drops commit-message trailers, so a `Closes #N` in a commit silently fails to close its issue. Where a branch has fixup commits, clean it up with `git rebase -i` before merging rather than re-enabling squash. `git bisect` can descend into a commit that never passed CI on its own: use `git bisect --first-parent`, and `git log --first-parent` for the PR-level view ([why](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/dotfiles/blob/main/agent/home/standards/github-standards.md#merge-methods))
- Watch CI until it passes
- **The owner merges.** Merge only the pull request he names, when he asks in this session. Never approve one
- Before pushing follow-up commits to a PR branch — or stating its state, or asking anything premised on it — check the PR is still open **now**, not from an earlier read. The owner often merges while work continues: if it has merged, create a new branch and PR instead

### Work Tracking

- **A description-depth or diff-depth change needs an issue before the work**, closed by `Closes #<n>` in the body. A title-depth change needs none; nor does a doc-sized correction a retro or end-session finds in its own repo: fix it there and name it in the retro. Hierarchy, dependencies and labels: [`docs/github-issues-workflow.md`](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/github-issues-workflow.md)
- **A read-back of just-written state is eventually consistent — wait before diagnosing.** When a just-written thing looks absent or unauthorised, wait and retry once before investigating, and treat "the platform is broken" as the last hypothesis: a new IAM binding reads as a bare permission denial for seconds to minutes ([why](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/agent-policy-rationale.md#a-read-back-of-just-written-state-lags))
- **Never use issue search for anything time-sensitive**: use issue listing or direct reads, and deduplicate against the full list, closed issues included ([why](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/github-issues-workflow.md#rules-for-agents))

### Decision records (ADR tiers)

Decisions are recorded at three tiers, personal, user and repo, per
[ADR-0015](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/dotfiles/blob/main/agent/adrs/0015-tiered-adrs.md).
User-tier ADRs bind every repo and are public at
[`agentic-coding-config/adrs/`](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/dotfiles/tree/main/agent/adrs):
consult them on demand, and never copy one into a repo. The rules for writing
one load when a file under `adrs/` or `decisions/` is read.

### Cross-Repo Work

- **Never edit files in a repo other than the one this session is working in.** Any direction, any repo pair: a project session editing `agentic-coding-config`, an `agentic-coding-config` session editing `dotfiles`, a `dotfiles` session editing `paul-context`. Cross-repo edits bypass the issue queue, skip that repo's review/PR flow, and pollute the current session's context with unrelated work. This holds even when the other repo is already cloned and writable, and even when the change is one line
- **File a detailed issue in the target repo instead.** "Detailed" means implementable without rediscovering anything: exact file paths, the full snippet to add, the rationale, every gotcha already ruled out, and acceptance criteria ([why](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/agent-policy-rationale.md#a-detailed-issue-is-the-cross-repo-route))
- **Before asserting how another repo behaves, read it.** Attaching a repo read-only is cheap and is the expected move, not a last resort: an issue, a policy line, or a skill body that describes another repo's behaviour is written from that repo's source, never inferred from what this one says about it — the estate's own docs are second-hand on that subject and go stale silently. a-c-c's README carried a copy of dotfiles' `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`, and the issue quoted the live file instead. Read it at origin's current head: fetch or pull a local clone first, and re-read issue or PR state rather than relying on what the session saw earlier. A clone behind origin is a second-hand copy too
- **Say what you filed.** Report the issue number back in the session summary so the cross-repo thread isn't lost

### Changing agent config

- **To request a change to agent configuration, open a GitHub issue against `pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config`**, from any surface, saying what should change and why. The config on disk is generated from fragments, so an edit in place is lost on the next apply ([why](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/agent-policy-rationale.md#config-changes-go-through-an-issue))

### Commit & PR Style

- Prefer several short paragraphs to one long line in commit messages; state what changed and why, not just what. End with `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Use that generic name even when a harness reminder names a model: the no-model-identifier rule covers every pushed artefact. In a public repo, what any artefact may say — commit, issue, PR, review — is [ADR-0022](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/dotfiles/blob/main/agent/adrs/0022-public-artefact-content.md)'s table

### Process Guidelines

- **3 strikes rule**: After 3 failed attempts debugging the same issue, stop and question the entire approach before trying again
- **Preview an irreversible batch read-only, then stop.** Before deleting, overwriting or force-pushing over a *set* of resources, list exactly what will be affected and stop for explicit confirmation. Suppress the *tool's* prompt (`--quiet`) but surface your own preview and wait: an instruction to run "without prompting" is about the tool, not the preview. Take the same care with a single destructive command on an absolute path outside your own scratch directory ([why](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/agent-policy-rationale.md#preview-an-irreversible-batch-then-stop))
- **Mask by allowlist, never by denylist.** When showing a config file, a log or a process command line that may carry secrets, print key names, counts or a named known-safe field. Never print whole lines with a list of known-secret keys masked: the list misses the key nobody thought of. A secret passed as a launch argument is the same trap: any log line that echoes the command line carries it
- **When a check reports nothing, prove it could have reported something.** Run it against a case that must produce a hit, then trust the empty result: an empty `grep` may mean the pattern is wrong ([why](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/agent-policy-rationale.md#a-silent-check-has-to-be-able-to-speak))
- **Lint before pushing**: run the relevant linter and test suite locally, and push only if everything passes
- **PR-stacking discipline**: claim "stacked on" only when the second branch literally has the first as parent, and keep a stacked PR a **draft** until its base merges ([the rest](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/context/rules/pr-stacking.md))
- **Web fetch blocked by a 403?** Some sites (UESP, Cloudflare-fronted wikis) reject an agent's User-Agent. Skip alternative URLs and go straight to `curl -sSL -A "<a desktop Safari UA>" "$URL" | pandoc -f html -t gfm --wrap=none`, then read or `grep` the markdown; save it as a per-project script if the site recurs

### Shell Scripts

- **Pass the non-interactive flag; an agent has no tty.** A command that stops to ask something waits forever, and the symptom is a hung session that reads as the model being slow, not an error: `apt-get -y`, `ssh`/`scp -o BatchMode=yes`. Do not pass `rm -f` reflexively: it also suppresses the errors you wanted to see ([why](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/agent-policy-rationale.md#pass-the-non-interactive-flag))
- **Verify CLI flags before using them — for both commands you run AND advice you give the user**: Run `<tool> --help` or `<tool> help <subcommand>` locally before committing or before recommending a flag in chat. `--no-lock`-style hallucinations waste a round-trip whether they fire in your own call or in the user's terminal after you suggest them

### Languages and stacks

- **New code, by kind** ([ADR-0027](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/dotfiles/blob/main/agent/adrs/0027-language-choice.md)): services, command-line tools and daemons in Go, standard library first; scripts in POSIX `sh`; anything in a browser in TypeScript. Extending an existing project uses that project's language, which overrides these defaults
- **Python only where it is clearly the best tool for the requirement** (machine learning, an AI library whose best-supported SDK is Python), and say why when you pick it. It is a dislike, not a ban
- **Front end: the lowest layer that fits** ([ADR-0026](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/dotfiles/blob/main/agent/adrs/0026-front-end-stack-standard.md)); a higher one needs a reason in the repo's own ADR. Content site (pages written ahead of time, no server logic): Hugo. Web app (a Go service with pages and some behaviour): Go-served HTML with TypeScript modules, bundled by esbuild and embedded in the binary
- Highly interactive app (mostly client state: an editor, a live multi-user view): React with TypeScript, built with Vite, served by the Go binary as a static bundle. Native: SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose, each a thin layer over a UI-free core. No htmx, Next.js or React Native
- Before building any UI, read the [style guide](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/style-guide.md) in full: the bar is a polished app, not a working one

## Ephemeral-first engineering

Portable policy, for any agent session on any surface. Agent sandboxes are
disposable: **how agents work must not depend on how long the environment
lives.** The reasoning behind each principle is in
[`docs/ephemeral-first.md`](https://github.com/pmgledhill102/agentic-coding-config/blob/main/docs/ephemeral-first.md).

1. **Environment-as-script.** Setup is committed, idempotent, and identical
   for a fresh environment and a resume. An install made mid-session to get
   unblocked is not finished until it is in the setup script, or in an issue
   asking for it.
2. **The repo is the default durable output channel, for what repos are
   for**: docs, scripts, code, configuration. Commit early rather than at the
   end. Datasets, fixtures, generated artifacts and bulk output do not belong
   in git; see 3.
3. **Durable storage is a separate, explicitly granted capability.** Never
   invent a location. If a task needs durable storage and none has been
   granted, say so and stop.
4. **Agent-built infrastructure checkpoints its state externally**, and so does
   anything else that records what exists.

Before ending a session, ask: **if this environment were destroyed right
now, what would be lost?** Every answer is something that should have been
committed, something that needs a granted durable store, or something that
was never worth keeping.

## Ubuntu

True only on **Ubuntu 24.04**: GNU userland, `/bin/sh` is dash. That covers
every cloud sandbox, and WSL (ADR-0020).

- **`apt-get update` first** on a fresh image

## Cloud sandbox

True only in an **ephemeral cloud sandbox**; the durable-machine fragment is
never composed into one — see ADR-0018 principle 5 and ADR-0020.

### This container is the whole environment

There is no chezmoi here, and `~/.claude/` is not chezmoi-managed.
`cloud/bootstrap.sh` writes most of it at build time, but the platform
launcher writes there too and refreshes its files each session, so presence
says nothing about age or owner — `~/.agents/.bootstrap-manifest` lists ours.

Anything installed by hand dies with the container and is invisible to the
next session. What must survive belongs in the repo or the setup script.

- **A session may start in the parent of its attached repos**, which are the subject:
  list and `git grep` them for the topic before answering from live probes or memory.

### Capabilities available here

- **Brokered Google Cloud access**, when `CREDENTIAL_BROKER_URL` is set.
  Request it with the `gcp-credentials` skill rather than asking a human to
  run `gcloud` by hand. The trigger is not "I need to change something in
  GCP" but **"I am about to assert something about live GCP state"**.
- **Skills delivered by the bootstrap** are the whole set — absent here means
  held back deliberately, not lost. Say so rather than improvising.
- **Docker** builds here go through the egress proxy: read `sandbox-docker` first.
- **A blocked host is not a dead end.** Ask for it: the proxy takes the new
  domain within seconds, though `WebFetch` may keep refusing until the session
  resumes, so retry with `curl` first. Re-test recorded blocks; they age badly.
- **`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` may be the literal `proxy-injected`**:
  the proxy cannot SigV4-sign, so check the key's shape before diagnosing IAM.

### `gh` is a property of the setup line

Prefer the GitHub MCP tools; otherwise `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/...` (REST) works for content, issues, PRs and runs
on `add_repo`-attached repos, but refuses settings, secrets, variables, alerts, Dependabot, keys, hooks, environments
and collaborators (use MCP) paths, `DELETE git/refs` and `--paginate` (page by hand); GraphQL-backed subcommands
(`gh issue list`, `gh pr list`, `gh pr view`, search), `/user/*` and `/orgs/*` are blocked. A denied `add_repo` is the
owner's call: ask once, naming the repo and what it unlocks, and do not proceed without it. Verify, never assume.
Confidently wrong here: **every GitHub request carries credentials, even a bare `curl`**, so a 200 says nothing about
visibility (read `.private`); **`git push --delete` prints "Everything up-to-date" and deletes nothing** (check
`git ls-remote --heads`). `gh`-backed helpers report `gh-unavailable` or `gh-unauthorized`: say what was not gathered,
never a clean result; a skill's `gh` command names the *operation*, so use the MCP call. `claude-code-remote` works
here; judge it by what a call returns, not by which kind of session you are. On an approval-binding failure
(anthropics/claude-code#90127, reported for child sessions), fall back to event-driven wakes via `github`.

## Claude Code adapter

Claude-specific guidance. The portable policy and the environment guidance
above are composed in from their own fragments; this section is only what
would be meaningless to Codex or OpenCode — Claude Code tool names, and the
MCP servers configured on this surface.

Anything portable belongs in the core fragment, not here.

### GitHub MCP

- **Prefer `mcp__github__*` tools over the `gh` CLI for all GitHub operations** when the GitHub MCP server is connected. Only fall back to `gh` if the MCP server is unavailable or a specific capability is missing
- **Three of them overflow the context limit unless called carefully.** `list_issues` must always be given `fields` — `["number", "title", "labels", "assignees", "state"]` costs around 750 tokens for a 36-issue repo, where an unfiltered call blows the limit somewhere past roughly 25 issues; never add `body`. One page of it is not the full list a dedup needs: filter server-side with `labels` to the candidate's `type:` label, or page to exhaustion via `pageInfo.endCursor`/`after`. `list_pull_requests` takes `fields` too: give it one and never include `body`, and pull detail for a single PR with `pull_request_read`. Their `state` values also differ in case — `list_issues` takes `"OPEN"`, `list_pull_requests` takes `"open"`. `issue_read` with method `get_sub_issues` has no field filter either, and every row carries a full body plus a full `repository` object, so `perPage` bounds the page but cannot make a row cheap; to count children, a plain `get` on the parent returns `sub_issues_summary` without fetching any
- **`gh` commands written into a skill or slash command are illustrative, not prescriptive.** Use the `mcp__github__*` equivalent when the MCP server is connected; fall back to `gh` where the MCP server is unavailable and `gh` is present. Which of the two exists is a property of the surface, so the environment fragment states it rather than this one. A literal command in an instruction otherwise overrides this preference at execution time, which is how a session ends up doing every discretionary GitHub op through MCP and every skill-driven one through the CLI

### Editing files

- **Batch reads before edits.** The Edit tool requires a prior Read of the file on older models and not on newer ones. When the model is unknown, read every target file first, then make all the edits — an unneeded read is cheap, and a refused parallel edit costs a round-trip

### Other MCP servers

Configured per-machine via `claude mcp add` and stored in `~/.claude.json`,
not in this repo. `home/settings.json.md` records which of their tools are
auto-approved and why.
